raw_text:
Below is a 12-week strength-focused programme for your client (34 F, intermediate lifter) starting 2026-06-01. I’ve phased training around her menstrual cycle pattern and the two flagged acyclic flare windows. Notes: flow days and flare days restrict intensity and impact — specifically: no HIIT, no heavy Valsalva, no jumping. Outside those days she is cleared for full training.

Assumptions/inputs used
- Cycle: 27-day cycle. Last period began 2026-05-04. Using 27-day cycle, the next periods (approx) begin: 2026-05-31, 2026-06-27, 2026-07-24, 2026-08-20, 2026-09-16. Her flow days last ~4 days each (day 1 = period start).
- Start date: 2026-06-01 (this is cycle day 2 for the 2026-05-31 period). I’ll align weekly plan with calendar dates to manage flare windows and flow days.
- Flare windows (no HIIT, no heavy Valsalva, no jumping): 2026-07-10 to 2026-07-13 and 2026-08-04 to 2026-08-07.
- Flow days always follow each period start for ~4 days.
- Client is intermediate — program uses progressive overload, 3–4 strength sessions/week plus accessory/recovery work.

High-level structure
- 12 weeks (2026-06-01 to 2026-08-23).
- Phases:
  - Weeks 1–4 (June): Foundation & volume, build technique and base strength. Emphasis on moderate intensity (RPE 6–8) with higher movement variety.
  - Weeks 5–8 (July): Strength block with heavier lifts and lower reps, but plan around the July flare (7/10–7/13) and flow days. Introduce scheduled taper during flare and flow.
  - Weeks 9–12 (Aug early–late): Peak/strength consolidation then a planned deload in final week. Account for Aug flare (8/4–8/7) and flow around 8/20–8/23.

Weekly training pattern (typical week outside flow/flare)
- 4 sessions per week: 2 lower-body focused (one strength heavy, one moderate volume), 2 upper-body / full-body sessions. Plus daily mobility and recovery.
- Alternate weeks with 3 sessions if client prefers (I’ll note how to combine).
- On flow days or flare days: reduce intensity and avoid heavy Valsalva and impact. Convert heavy days into technique / mobility / lighter load sessions with focus on tempo, higher reps with lighter loads, unilateral work, and low-impact conditioning (walking, cycling, deep breathing). Avoid max or near-max sets.

Progression and intensity
- Week 1–4: 6–12 RM ranges, 3–4 sets most main lifts. Focus on tempo and form.
- Week 5–8: 3–6 RM for primary lifts on heavy days (except for scheduled flow/flare adjustments). Increased load, lower volume.
- Week 9–11: Peaking / consolidation — moderate-high loads with slightly reduced volume.
- Week 12: Deload/recovery: lower volume and intensity to allow adaptation.

Nutrition and recovery guidance (general; adapt to client needs)
- Calories: maintain or slight surplus for strength gain depending on client goal (not specified). Recommend 0–+250 kcal from maintenance if aiming to add strength without unwanted fat.
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg bodyweight per day.
- Hydration: prioritize, especially during cycle and flare days. Small frequent fluids and electrolytes if heavy symptoms.
- Micronutrients: ensure adequate iron (monitor menstruation-related losses), vitamin D, magnesium. Consider discussing supplements with client’s clinician if deficiency suspected.
- Sleep: target 7–9 hours.
- Pain/flare management: plan gentle mobility, diaphragmatic breathing, heat packs, NSAIDs only as prescribed by clinician. Encourage tracking symptom patterns and training tolerance.

How cycle and flare windows are handled
- Flow days (days 1–4 after period start) each cycle: treat those days as low-moderate intensity. Avoid heavy 1RM attempts, high intra-abdominal pressure (heavy Valsalva) and jumping. Replace with lighter, controlled lifts, more unilateral work or machines, and higher rep sets (8–15) with lighter loads.
- Flare windows:
  - 2026-07-10 to 2026-07-13 (Week 6): change scheduled sessions during that week to low-impact, non-Valsalva, no jumping; maintain movement but scaled.
  - 2026-08-04 to 2026-08-07 (Week 10): similar modified week.
- If symptoms present outside these windows, use same rules and apply autoregulation.

Program week-by-week (calendar dates included). Each session lists exercises, sets x reps, tempo and notes. RPE scale: 1–10 (aim RPE given). If a session falls on flow or flare days, the version to perform is provided.

Week 1 — 2026-06-01 to 06-06 (Cycle day context: period started 5/31; 6/1 = day 2 — flow day)
Overview: Foundation—focus on technique, moderate loads. Because 6/1–6/03 are flow days, first 3 training days adjusted.

Week 1 schedule (4 sessions: Mon/ Tue/Thu/Sat recommended; shift if needed)
Session A (Lower — flow-modified) — 6/1 (flow)
- Warm-up: 8–10 min bike, pelvic/hip mobility, diaphragmatic breathing
- Goblet squat: 3 x 8–10 @ RPE 6 (light-moderate)
- Romanian deadlift (dumbbell or light barbell): 3 x 8 @ RPE 6–7 (no heavy Valsalva; exhale on exertion)
- Split stance cable row or single-arm DB row: 3 x 10 each
- Glute bridge (floor or bench) controlled tempo 3:0:2: 3 x 12
- Pallof press (anti-rotation): 2 x 12 each side
- Low-impact finisher: 10–15 min brisk walk or bike, steady
Notes: avoid heavy breath-holding and any jumping.

Session B (Upper — flow-modified)
- Warm-up: band pull-aparts, scapular mobility
- Incline DB press: 3 x 8–10
- Lat pulldown or assisted pull-up: 3 x 8–10
- Seated DB shoulder press: 3 x 8–10 (avoid maximal Valsalva)
- Chest-supported T-bar or incline row: 3 x 10
- Farmer carry (light): 3 x 40–60 m
- Core: dead bug 3 x 12
Notes: Light–moderate loads. No heavy pushing near max.

Session C (Lower — technique/volume) — Thu
- Warm-up: hip circles, bodyweight squats
- Front squat (light): 4 x 6 @ RPE 6–7
- Single-leg RDL: 3 x 8 each
- Leg press or belt squat (if available): 3 x 10
- Bulgarian split squat: 3 x 8 each
- Standing calf raise: 3 x 12–15
- Mobility & breathing 10 min
Notes: Emphasize tempo and spinal neutrality.

Session D (Upper — conditioning, low-impact) — Sat
- Warm-up
- Bent-over row: 4 x 6–8
- Flat DB press: 3 x 8–10
- Face pulls: 3 x 12–15
- Lat-focused cable row: 3 x 10
- Core: side plank 3 x 30–45 sec
- Low-impact steady-state: 15–20 min bike or walk

Week 2 — 2026-06-07 to 06-13
Cycle context: period ended ~6/03; from 6/07 she is early follicular → mid-follicular (energy rising). Full sessions allowed (not flow). No flare windows yet.

Aim: increase volume and intensity slightly.

Session A (Lower — strength)
- Back squat: 4 x 6 @ RPE 7–8
- RDL: 4 x 6–8
- Leg press: 3 x 10
- Nordic/hamstring curl or hamstring curl machine: 3 x 8–10
- Ab wheel or plank variations: 3 x 30–45s
- 5–10 min mobility

Session B (Upper — strength)
- Barbell bench press: 4 x 6 @ RPE 7–8 (avoid breath-holding—teach exhale on concentric)
- Pull-ups / weighted assisted: 4 x 6–8
- Seated DB shoulder press: 3 x 8
- Chest-supported row: 3 x 8–10
- Farmer carry: 3 x 40m
- Banded face pulls: 3 x 15

Session C (Lower — volume/hypertrophy)
- Front squat or goblet: 4 x 8–10
- Bulgarian split squat: 3 x 10 each
- Good mornings (light-moderate): 3 x 10
- Calf raises: 4 x 12
- Glute-ham raise or reverse hyper: 3 x 8–10

Session D (Upper / full body)
- Incline bench: 3 x 8
- Barbell row: 4 x 6–8
- Romanian deadlift (lighter): 3 x 8
- Single-arm DB press: 3 x 10 each
- Core circuit: 2 rounds (pallof, dead bug, bird dog)

Week 3 — 2026-06-14 to 06-20
Context: mid-follicular → ovulatory phase (higher energy). Good time for heavier sessions and slightly higher intensity. Continue 4 sessions. Introduce heavier sets for primary lifts.

Session structure: same split as Week 2 but increase one top set intensity by ~2.5–5% or add a top set at lower rep range (e.g., 5RM).

Key lifts:
- Back squat: 5 x 5 @ RPE 7.5–8
- Bench press: 5 x 5
- Deadlift (conventional or trap bar): 3 x 5 @ RPE 7–8 (ensure bracing but avoid breath-holding if symptomatic — coach breathing technique)

Accessory and conditioning: maintain low-impact steady cardio 10–15 min after sessions.

Week 4 — 2026-06-21 to 06-27
Context: luteal pre-menstrual approaching toward period on 6/27. Slightly higher fatigue risk late week; autoregulate. Continue progressive overload but add more intentional recovery day if energy drops.

Session emphasis: maintain strength but reduce accessory volume if needed. Include 1 mobility + restorative session (yoga, breathing, light walking).

Week 5 — 2026-06-28 to 07-04
Context: Period expected 2026-06-27 start → flow on 6/27–6/30 (so first 1–4 days of this week are flow). Then mid-week energy rising. Keep first 2–3 days low impact if client still on flow.

This week begins heavy strength preparation for upcoming Week 6 (which includes first flare on 7/10 later). Increase heaviness when not on flow.

Sessions similar to Week 3 but plan heavy session earlier in week when not flow.

Week 6 — 2026-07-05 to 07-11 (IMPORTANT: flare window 2026-07-10 to 07-13)
Context: this week contains flare onset Friday 7/10. Plan heavy work earlier in week (Mon–Thu). Friday–Mon must be modified.

Week 6 schedule recommendations:
- Monday 7/06: Heavy Lower (before flare)
  - Back squat: 5 x 4 @ RPE 8 (heaviest planned this block)
  - Deadlift (trap bar): 3 x 4–5 @ RPE 7.5
  - Hip thrust: 3 x 6–8
  - Light core work
  Note: Coach cues to avoid maximal breath-holding; teach exhale on ascent and bracing without full Valsalva as needed.
- Tuesday 7/07: Heavy Upper
  - Bench press: 5 x 4 @ RPE 8
  - Weighted pull-up or rows: 4 x 6
  - Overhead press: 3 x 6
  - Accessory sets
- Thursday 7/09: Moderate full-body / volume (last full session before flare window)
  - Front squat: 4 x 6
  - Romanian deadlift: 3 x 6–8
  - Incline press: 3 x 8
  - Rowing movement: 3 x 8–10

Flare window adjustment (Fri 7/10 to Mon 7/13)
- During 7/10–7/13: NO HIIT, NO heavy Valsalva, NO JUMPING. Convert scheduled sessions into low-load movement-focused sessions:
  - Mobility, band work, light unilateral strength (DB goblet squat, lunges with RPE 5–6), machines (leg press, chest press) with reduced loads and higher reps (10–15).
  - Emphasize breathing: diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic floor awareness, avoid breath-holding on exertion.
  - Keep aerobic work low-impact: walking, cycling, swimming at conversational pace.
  - Example session (7/11):
    - Warm-up 10 min brisk walk
    - Leg press: 3 x 12–15 @ RPE 5–6
    - Seated row: 3 x 12
    - Glute bridge with band: 3 x 15
    - Pallof press: 3 x 12 each
    - Finish with 10–15 min gentle bike or stretching
- If symptoms are severe, prioritize rest and clinician advice.

Week 7 — 2026-07-12 to 07-18
Context: flare window ends 7/13. Allow a return-to-load progression: mid-week re-introduction to heavier loads if client feels recovered. Note that period expected 2026-07-24 (so currently mid-luteal).

Progression:
- Start week with two moderate sessions (Mon/Tue), then heavy lower or heavy upper on Thu if tolerated.
- Re-introduce heavier sets gradually (reduce top set loads by ~10% first session back).

Week 8 — 2026-07-19 to 07-25
Context: period due 7/24 — flow days 7/24–7/27 (this overlaps Week 8 end). Plan heavier sessions earlier in week (Mon–Thu) and reduce intensity on flow days. End-of-week sessions modified if overlapping flow.

Outline:
- Monday 7/19: Heavy lower (squats/dl) 4 x 5
- Tuesday 7/20: Heavy upper 4 x 5–6
- Thursday 7/22: Volume lower/hypertrophy 3–4 x 8–10
- Saturday 7/24: Flow day — convert planned session to light mobility + machine-based moderate effort

Week 9 — 2026-07-26 to 08-01
Context: post-period recovery; follicular rising energy. This week is a good block to rebuild intensity — aim for heavier top sets again. No flare this week.

Typical sessions:
- Continue 4 sessions: heavy lower, heavy upper, volume lower, upper accessory.
- Introduce 1 targeted unilateral day (for imbalance correction): e.g., single-leg RDLs, Bulgarian split squats.

Week 10 — 2026-08-02 to 08-08 (IMPORTANT: flare window 2026-08-04 to 08-07)
Context: flare 8/4–8/7 falls mid-week. Period expected next on 8/20 so not overlapping. Plan heavy sessions early in week (Mon/Tue) and modify mid-week through the flare.

Plan:
- Monday 8/02: Heavy full lower or squat 5 x 3–5 (go relatively heavy early)
- Tuesday 8/03: Heavy upper
- Wed–Sat (8/04–8/07): Flare days — modify sessions to low-impact, low-Valsalva format (same approach as earlier flare). Focus on mobility, machine-based work at RPE 5–6, higher reps.
- Sun 8/08: Light recovery / active rest

Example modified session during flare:
- Warm-up: 10 min easy bike, pelvic mobility
- Cable hip thrusts: 3 x 12
- Seated leg curl: 3 x 12
- Seated chest press: 3 x 12
- Lat pulldown: 3 x 12
- Core: side plank 3 x 30–45s
- Finish: 10–15 min gentle walk

Week 11 — 2026-08-09 to 08-15
Context: post-flare recovery — reintroduce heavier loading gradually. Energy likely good in mid-follicular. Aim to consolidate strength gains with moderate-high loads.

Sessions:
- Monday: Heavy lower 4 x 4 or 5 x 3
- Tuesday: Heavy upper 4 x 5
- Thursday: Volume lower 3–4 x 8–10
- Saturday: Upper volume/accessory, unilateral work

Week 12 — 2026-08-16 to 08-22 (Deload week ends 8/23)
Context: period expected 8/20 → flow 8/20–8/23. Plan a deload this week (lower volume and intensity), especially since period and flow overlap. Use this week for recovery, technique, and mobility.

Deload guidelines:
- Reduce volume by 40–60% and intensity by ~20–30% across lifts.
- Keep sessions 2–3 short workouts focusing on movement quality, breathing, light unilateral work.
- Examples:
  - Session 1: Light squat 3 x 5 @ RPE 5–6; RDL 2 x 6; core + mobility.
  - Session 2: Light bench 3 x 5; rows 3 x 6–8; band work.
  - Daily walking and extra sleep.

Autoregulation and coaching cues
- Use RPE or daily readiness questionnaires. If pelvic or abdominal pain increases, reduce load, avoid valsalva, stop heavy pushing and jumping.
- For heavy lifts teach breathing pattern: inhale into belly, bracing and controlled exhale on concentric; if client finds Valsalva increases pain, reduce load and avoid maximal breath-hold.
- Consider using belt sparingly only when necessary and not on flare/flow days.
- Prioritize single-leg work and posterior-chain strengthening to support pelvic health.
- If symptoms of flare are severe or red flags emerge (fever, unusual bleeding), pause training and refer to clinician.

Sample microcycle templates (non-flow / non-flare heavy week)
- Day 1: Lower heavy
  - Back squat: 5 x 4
  - Romanian deadlift: 4 x 6
  - Bulgarian split squat: 3 x 8 each
  - Glute bridge: 3 x 8–10
  - Core: pallof 3 x 12 each
- Day 2: Upper heavy
  - Bench press: 5 x 4
  - Weighted pull-ups / rows: 4 x 6
  - Overhead press: 3 x 6
  - Face pulls: 3 x 12
- Day 3: Lower volume
  - Front squat 4 x 6–8
  - Deadlift variant 3 x 6
  - Leg press 3 x 12
  - Calves + mobility
- Day 4: Upper volume / accessory
  - Incline DB press 3 x 8–10
  - Barbell row 4 x 6–8
  - Lateral raises / rotator cuff 3 x 12
  - Core circuit 3 rounds

Sample flare/flow session (always)
- Warm-up: 10 min light cardio and pelvic/hip mobility
- 3–4 machine-based or DB unilateral exercises x 3 sets of 12–15 at RPE 5–6
- 10–20 min low-impact conditioning (walking, bike)
- Finish with mobility, diaphragmatic breathing, and pelvic floor relaxation drills

Key exercises prioritized
- Squats (back/front/goblet)
- Deadlift variants (Romanian, trap bar)
- Hip thrusts/glute bridges
- Split squats/Bulgarian split
- Bench press/incline DB press
- Rows/pull-ups/lat pulldown
- Overhead press and scapular control
- Core stability work (Pallof, dead bug, side planks) rather than heavy loaded axial compression during flow/flare.

Monitoring and adjustments
- Track symptoms daily and adjust on the fly; always err on the side of reducing intensity and impact during flare and flow days.
- If pain increases during a lift, stop and regress to lighter variation or machine.
- Re-test main lifts (5RM or 3RM) after a recovery block (e.g., end of Week 8 or Week 11) rather than during or immediately after a flare.

Final notes for the trainer
- Keep communication open about symptoms and perceived exertion each session.
- Emphasize breathing technique to reduce intra-abdominal pressure when client is comfortable.
- Use the flare windows as planned recovery periods — maintain movement but avoid pushing heavy on those dates.
- If the client has additional medical guidance from a gynecologist/surgeon, align modifications with that advice.

If you want, I can:
- Convert the calendar plan into a printable weekly schedule with checkboxes.
- Provide specific progressions with weekly % loads for main lifts based on a tested 1RM/5RM.
- Create alternative 3-day-per-week versions or hypertrophy-biased variations.
